Life insurance proceeds a corporation receives on a death are added to its capital dividend account (Income Tax Act 89(1), capital dividend account, paragraph (d))
facts.value: Added to the capital dividend account: the proceeds of a life insurance policy received by the corporation in consequence of the death of any person, less the policy's adjusted cost basis immediately before the death (see cda_life_insurance_acb_deduction)

facts.title: The policy's adjusted cost basis immediately before the death is taken off the proceeds added to the capital dividend account (Income Tax Act 89(1), capital dividend account, subparagraph (d)(iii))
facts.value: Subtracted from the life insurance proceeds added to the capital dividend account: the adjusted cost basis (as defined in 148(9)), immediately before the death, of the policyholder's interest in the policy (deaths after March 21, 2016)

facts.title: A dividend a private corporation elects to be a capital dividend is not included in the shareholder's income (Income Tax Act 83(2))
facts.value: When a private corporation elects for the full amount of a dividend (in prescribed manner and form, on time), the dividend is a capital dividend to the extent of its capital dividend account immediately before it became payable, and no part of it is included in computing the income of any shareholder

facts.title: What the Ontario surtax is figured on, the gross tax amount, and where the Ontario dividend tax credit comes in (Taxation Act, 2007 (Ontario) 16(2))
facts.value: The surtax is figured on the gross tax amount: basic Ontario tax less the non-refundable credits in subdivision b, plus additional taxes (sections 11 and 12), less the credits in subdivision d. The Ontario dividend tax credit (section 19.1, subdivision g) is not among them, so it comes off after the surtax
